gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Wuben X5's 4.44 Wh cell holds about 400 lm for about 100 minutes once turbo steps down. That is roughly 670 lumen-hours per charge, measured by BudgetLightForum reviewer roma58, which works out to about 0.98 Wh per ounce of light.
standout_why: Of the rival pages, I could only read our own dealectric.com page. It gives the X5 as '1,200 mAh' and '~400 lm sustained', but has no Wh figure, no time spent at that sustained level, and no per-charge or per-ounce number. The Popular Mechanics ArkPro Ultra review (cited) blocked fetching, and so did the Olight, Lowe's PDF, Adorama, Fenix, Battery Junction and Wuben store pages, so I could not check those rivals. In the ChatGPT answers, the only runtime language is 'Lumens are advertised peak outputs, not sustained brightness', with no sustained duration for any pick. The finding is new, but I could compute it for only one candidate, so it confirms one pick rather than ranking them.
decides: It supports the X5's 'best replaceable battery' slot with a concrete number: about 100 minutes of usable ~400 lm light, or about 2 hours at 350 lm, from a 4.44 Wh swappable cell. A spare cell doubles that. It cannot yet rank the X5 against the ArkPro or ArkPro Ultra. Those have a 2,000 mAh sealed cell per our page, but I could not open a page giving their voltage, Wh or measured sustained output, so a per-charge comparison is still open.
